verification.scope: Execution and contract checks; business ambiguities require operator answers

notes: Only one table was detected (sheet 'Variants', header row 0, 12 data rows). Each row is one variant SKU and produces exactly one product record with exactly one /prices entry (price_list 'standard'), so /prices identity keys (price_list, effective_from) are naturally unique per product.
Currency is explicit in the source as 'PHP' for every row; the schema default THB must not be applied. No FX conversion is performed.

Tax evidence is explicit: 'Tax included' = No (vat_included false) and 'Tax rate' = 5% (vat_rate 0.05 as a fraction, not 5). These are fixture values; nothing is inferred from the PHP currency or a country rule.
No effective_from / effective_to date columns exist in this workbook, so those optional price fields stay null; there is no basis to invent validity dates.
No pack size column exists; /unit/pack_size stays null. Sales unit 'PAIR' already matches the target enum_hint, so unit_normalize should be a no-op.

No status, barcode, brand, description, inventory, promotion or category columns exist in this file. Status should take the explicit schema default 'active'; inventory and promotions arrays stay empty rather than being invented.

Schema fields /attributes is an open object with additionalProperties of scalar types only: Color, EU size and Parent style can be preserved there via attributes_passthrough + SourceSpec.rename (color, size, parent_style). Nested attribute objects cannot be expressed.

Column 'Tax rate' was detected as a float with the value shown as '5%', so the mapping must parse it as a percentage rather than reading the literal 5.0 — a scale check against the sample output would confirm it.
Column 'Parent style' is not a product category hierarchy; mapping it to /category would require inventing a category semantics, so it is retained as an attribute.

tables.reason: Sheet 'Variants' is a one-row-per-variant SKU master: SKU is unique across all 12 rows (unique_ratio 1.0), carries the required identity/product_name fields, and each row additionally supplies a single standard price with its currency, tax flag and tax rate. That makes it the product/variant table with an embedded (single-row) price record rather than a standalone pricing table.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Header 'SKU'; 12 distinct values for 12 rows, all sku_like (STYLE-1-BLK-40 …). Structure encodes parent style + color + size, which matches the operator statement that one record = one variant SKU and parent style is not the identity.

columns.name: Product name
columns.reason: Header 'Product name'; 3 style-level names repeated once per variant (SIM court shoe 1/2/3), i.e. the display name of the product each variant belongs to.

columns.name: Currency
columns.reason: Header 'Currency'; single explicit value 'PHP' in all 12 rows. This is explicit source evidence and overrides the schema default of THB, so it is mapped rather than defaulted.

columns.name: Sales unit
columns.reason: Header 'Sales unit'; single explicit value 'PAIR' in all 12 rows, which is already one of the enum_hint values (PCS, PACK, …, PAIR), so no unit conversion is needed.

columns.name: Price list
columns.reason: Header 'Price list'; single explicit value 'standard' across all rows, matching the operator instruction to use price_list 'standard' where explicitly stated.

columns.name: Net price
columns.reason: Header 'Net price'; always populated, price_like, 12 distinct values 1234.56–1356.77. It is the per-variant unit price that belongs inside the single /prices entry created from this row.

columns.name: Tax included
columns.reason: Header 'Tax included' with boolean-like values; all 12 rows say 'No', so the price is VAT-exclusive and vat_included maps to false (required field, satisfied by explicit source data, not convention).

columns.name: Tax rate
columns.reason: Header 'Tax rate'; single value '5%' in all rows, read as a percentage. It must be parsed to the fraction 0.05 (parse_number_th with percent_to_fraction) to match the vat_rate default of 0.07's scale. The 5% is a fixture value taken as given; it is not inferred from country or brand.

columns.name: Parent style
columns.reason: Header 'Parent style'; 3 distinct values (STYLE-1/2/3) each repeating 4 times, i.e. the style grouping above the variant. It is not the identity and is not a product category, so it is retained as an extra attribute (attributes_passthrough with a rename to parent_style) rather than published as /category.

columns.name: Color
columns.reason: Header 'Color'; 2 distinct code values (BLK, WHT) that also appear as the second token of the SKU. The operator explicitly requires Color to be preserved as attributes.color strings.

columns.name: EU size
columns.reason: Header 'EU size'; integer 40/41, matching the last token of the SKU. The operator explicitly requires EU size to be preserved as attributes.size strings.

changes_from_draft: Changed /prices/*/price_list from a constant to the explicit source column 'Price list' (value 'standard' on all rows).
Changed /prices/*/vat_included from const false to parse_bool('Tax included') with default false; every source row says 'No'.
Added /prices/*/vat_rate from 'Tax rate' using parse_number_th(percent_to_fraction=true), so '5%' becomes 0.05.

Added SourceSpec.rename Color→color, EU size→size, Parent style→parent_style so attributes_passthrough emits attributes.color, attributes.size and attributes.parent_style. Parent style is retained as an attribute, not mapped to /category.
Mapped /status to the contract's explicit default 'active' because the file has no status column.
Left /prices/*/effective_from and /prices/*/effective_to null: the workbook has no date columns, so validity dates are not invented.
No inventory, promotions, barcode, brand, description or pack-size source columns exist; those optional fields/arrays are omitted rather than fabricated.
Currency is explicit PHP in the file, so the schema default THB is not used and no FX conversion is performed. Sales unit PAIR already matches the target enum.
Attributes passthrough cannot cast a numeric EU size to string; if the source reads EU size as numeric, it remains numeric under /attributes, which the open attributes schema permits.
